front: Feature missing, or feature not licensed?
back: Sales Premium and Enterprise differ in which AI capabilities are included. Check the plan before debugging the configuration. Keyword: absent, not broken.

front: A mailbox configured but not approved
back: Does not sync at all, and the failure is reported on the mailbox record rather than to the user. Approve, test, then enable. Keyword: approval is a separate step.

front: Why an AI feature produces empty output
back: Conversational intelligence, timelines, and Copilot summaries all read synchronised activity. A broken mailbox surfaces two layers above as a thin summary. Keyword: check sync first.

front: Does a business process flow enforce the sequence?
back: No. It is guidance and visibility. A flow, an import, or the API can still write out of order. Keyword: guidance, not enforcement.

front: Set duplicate detection before the bulk load
back: A duplicated lead and account estate degrades scoring, routing, and every agent reasoning over the records. Keyword: duplicates poison the AI.

front: Removing a seller's excess access
back: Dataverse security is additive with no deny, so remove the role granting it. Adding a restrictive role can only widen. Keyword: remove, never add.

front: An agent that sees more than its seller
back: A shared connection or elevated service identity lets an agent summarise records the requester cannot see. The summary is a leak dressed as a feature. Keyword: agents inherit an identity.

front: Retire a product, do not delete it
back: Only active products can be added to new records, and a retired product stays on historical ones. Deleting breaks history. Keyword: withdraw by retiring.

front: The cost of write-in products
back: They carry no product id, so revenue against them cannot be analysed by product. Heavy use means the catalogue does not match what you sell. Keyword: unreportable revenue.

front: Copilot feature or agent?
back: Copilot summarises and drafts and needs a seller present. An agent acts without one being started. Keyword: assist, or act.

front: Why the data model is the foundation
back: Scoring, routing, forecasting, and agent research all degrade the same way on duplicates, missing relationships, and free-text decision fields. Keyword: AI reads your model.

front: Extend standard tables, do not duplicate them
back: First-party AI features understand the standard model. A parallel custom table is invisible to them. Keyword: stay on the standard schema.

front: Sales dashboard or Power BI?
back: Dashboards answer 'what next' against live records with row-level security. Power BI answers analytical questions across volume and systems — embed it. Keyword: operational vs analytical.

front: What agent capacity is consumed by
back: Actions, not users. An agent turned loose on a large estate consumes in proportion to the records it touches. Keyword: volume, not headcount.

front: The pilot that lies about cost
back: 200 leads for a month, then a month's allocation gone in a week against 20,000. Estimate from volume before rollout. Keyword: pilots do not scale linearly in your favour.

front: What sequences do in the Sales accelerator
back: Attach a defined cadence of steps to a lead or opportunity and surface the next one due, so the methodology becomes the interface. Keyword: work the list.

front: Assignment rule order
back: Rules are evaluated in order, so a broad rule above a specific one absorbs everything. Define a fallback or records sit unassigned. Keyword: specific rules go first.

front: Conversational intelligence produces nothing
back: Usually recording, consent, or an unsupported language and channel — not configuration. Calls must actually be captured. Keyword: no recording, no insight.

front: Why predictive scoring needs losses
back: The model learns from closed history of both kinds. A tenant that deletes losses instead of marking them lost concludes everything succeeds. Keyword: record the losses.

front: What relationship intelligence depends on
back: Mailbox synchronisation and activity tracking. It computes health and who-knows-whom from interaction history that must exist. Keyword: no activity, no relationship.

front: Forecast adjustments do not overwrite
back: A manual adjustment is recorded alongside the rolled-up figure, so judgement stays visible and auditable rather than silently replacing the data. Keyword: adjustment is additive.

front: Lead vs opportunity
back: A lead is interest and is disposable. An opportunity is a deal being worked. Qualifying creates the account, contact, and opportunity. Keyword: interest becomes a deal.

front: Why disqualify rather than delete
back: A disqualified lead with a reason is training data for scoring. A deleted lead is nothing at all. Keyword: keep the negatives.

front: Qualification criteria as fields, not notes
back: Budget, authority, need, and timeline as structured choices are readable by scoring, routing, and agents. In a note they are invisible to all three. Keyword: structure it or lose it.

front: Target leakage in a scoring model
back: Including a field only populated once the outcome is known gives excellent reported accuracy and no predictive value — it is reading the answer. Keyword: exclude the tell.

front: Why a score does not move when you edit a field
back: Scores refresh on a schedule and models retrain periodically. A score ranks a queue; it does not judge a record live. Keyword: recent estimate, not live calculation.

front: Research-only vs Research and engage
back: Research-only gathers and briefs, leaving all contact to a human. Engage lets the agent correspond with the prospect itself. Keyword: does it talk to customers?

front: Who owns the engage-mode decision
back: Whoever owns brand and compliance — an autonomous system is corresponding in the organisation's name. Not a technical choice. Keyword: engage is a business decision.

front: Why the agent's trail matters
back: It records what it researched and why, which is what makes a seller's disagreement resolvable rather than a matter of opinion. Keyword: show the basis.

front: Two things to monitor on an agent
back: Quality — do its conclusions hold up against what sellers find — and consumption as volume changes. Keyword: is it right, and what does it cost?

front: System-calculated vs user-entered revenue
back: System-calculated keeps the total honest against the line items and is the right default. User-entered is the seller's number, chosen deliberately. Keyword: who owns the total?

front: An overridden price stops following the list
back: A price list update never reaches an overridden line. That is where reconciliation surprises hide. Keyword: override breaks the link.

front: What the pipeline view is for
back: A board by stage with inline editing and aggregates — the surface managers work in. Choose columns supporting the next action, not every field. Keyword: next action, not everything.

front: What the Sales Opportunity Agent watches
back: Open opportunities: stalled stages, unanswered threads, close dates approaching with no activity. Keyword: pipeline hygiene without a manager reading everything.

front: Why the Opportunity Agent reports false silence
back: 'Nothing has happened' is only true if what happened was tracked. Untracked email makes the agent cry wolf and sellers ignore it. Keyword: tracking before agents.

front: The Sales Close Agent's intended posture
back: Collaboration, not autonomy. It operates where money and commitments are, so it proposes and prepares and a named human decides. Keyword: propose, human disposes.

front: How to tell if the Close Agent is working
back: Measure whether its interventions shorten cycles, not whether it generates activity. Activity without movement is measurable as such. Keyword: cycle time, not volume.

front: What the Sales Research Agent is for
back: Preparation — the hour before a meeting spent on account history, recent news, and the last exchanges. It researches; it does not act. Keyword: brief, not act.

front: Which Sales agent does not take action
back: The Sales Research Agent. Qualification, Opportunity, and Close all act; Research assembles a briefing. Keyword: research is read-only.

front: Why the research canvas matters
back: A briefing nobody can interrogate has saved no time. The canvas is for exploring findings and following a thread, not reading a static report. Keyword: interrogable output.

front: Internal and external research must be distinguished
back: Internal findings trace to records; external ones are only as good as the source. Mixed without labels, a seller repeats an unverified claim to a customer. Keyword: label the provenance.

front: Line discount or opportunity discount?
back: Both exist and they reconcile differently. Know which the organisation uses before anyone reconciles a forecast. Keyword: agree the discount level.

front: Interpreting an agent's actions
back: Read the trail — what it did, against which records, on what basis. That is what turns a complaint into a configuration change. Keyword: evidence, then adjust.

front: Which agent belongs to which stage
back: Qualification at the top of the funnel, Opportunity through the middle, Close at the end, Research alongside all three. Keyword: funnel position picks the agent.

front: What the Sales mobile app is for
back: The moments around a meeting — preparation, notes, quick updates — not full record editing. Keyword: before and after the meeting.

front: Offline needs planning
back: Which tables are available offline is configured. A record outside the offline profile is missing at exactly the wrong moment. Keyword: choose the offline tables.

front: Why Teams calling matters for AI
back: Calling from a record logs the call against it, which is what makes call activity reliable enough for conversational intelligence. Keyword: logged calls feed the analysis.

front: SMS is a contact from the organisation
back: It carries consent and record-keeping obligations and belongs on the timeline like any other activity. Keyword: consent and timeline.

front: The cost of an embedded canvas app
back: A second application to maintain, license, and secure. It must earn its place against configuring the form properly. Keyword: embedding is not free.

front: Embedded Power BI uses its own security
back: It honours the Power BI model, not Dataverse row-level security, so it can show aggregates a seller could never query directly. Keyword: different security boundary.
